chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them)...

...regarding a man who forgot to enter the state of Ihram or was unaware, and he had performed all the rituals, circumambulated, and performed Sa'ee. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His intention suffices him if he had intended that, so his Hajj is complete, even if he did not recite the Talbiyya.'
And he (peace be upon him) said regarding a patient who fainted until the time came: 'He enters Ihram from it.'

key_terms.إحرام: Ihram: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.سعى: Sa'ee: Walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.هل: Halla: To recite the Talbiyya aloud to enter Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to enter Ihram before performing Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle that intention (niyyah) is the core of worship, validating Hajj for those who forgot or were ignorant of Ihram as long as the internal resolve existed. It further clarifies the ruling for a person who fainted before the Miqat, establishing that they must assume the state of Ihram from their current location upon regaining consciousness, reflecting the flexibility of ritual purity and state in cases of incapacity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)

regarding a man who forgot that he should be wearing Ihraam, or did not know, and he had witnessed the rituals, all of them, and circumambulated, and performed Sa’ee. Heasws said: ‘His intention would suffice him when he had intended that. Thus, his Hajj would be complete, and even if he had not exclaimed Talbiyya’.
And heasws said regarding a man who had fainted until he came to the juncture. So heasws said: ‘He should wear Ihraam from it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from certain persons of our people

who has said the following: “If one forgets to assume the state of Ihram or is ignorant, attends all places for performing the acts of al-Hajj such as Tawaf, Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah and so on, one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘His intention is sufficient. If he had such intention, his Hajj is complete even though he did not say Talbiyah.’
About the case of a man who fainted due to illness until Miqat (place for assuming the state of Ihram), he (the Imam) said, ‘He must assume the state of Ihram.’”
